object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person receiving care at the clinic, identified by a patient ID

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient, and a patient can have many appointments. Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a patient, printed on their clinic card

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who examines patients during appointments

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments. Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a doctor, assigned by the medical licensing authority

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical specialty area practiced by a doctor, such as cardiology or general practice

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled meeting between a patient and a doctor at the clinic

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for an appointment, generated when the appointment is created

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: Date
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment is scheduled

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time slot for scheduling appointments, such as 09:00 or 09:30

source_references.excerpt: we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The status of an appointment, constrained to one of four values

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled. An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason given by the patient when booking the appointment

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A note attached by the doctor after the appointment visit

source_references.excerpt: after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A room at the clinic used for patient examinations

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.definition: A unique identifier for an exam room

ambiguities.description: Scheduling constraint clarity: The transcript states appointments are 'on a date and at a time slot' with 'fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30', but does not explicitly state whether a Doctor can have multiple appointments on the same Date at the same TimeSlot, or whether the combination of Date + TimeSlot must be unique across all appointments. This affects whether a composite uniqueness constraint should be applied across Appointment-Date-TimeSlot or if additional fact types (e.g., tracking room assignments) are needed to prevent scheduling conflicts.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: Doctor-room assignment: The transcript mentions exam rooms with room numbers but does not state whether appointments are assigned to specific rooms, or how rooms relate to doctors and appointments. It is unclear whether this is a tracked relationship or a logistical detail handled outside the core data model.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

ambiguities.description: Optional visit reason: The transcript states 'An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking', using the word 'can', which suggests optionality. This has been modeled as optional (no mandatory constraint), but it is not explicitly confirmed whether all visit reasons are recorded or whether some appointments may be booked without a stated reason.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

ambiguities.description: Primary doctor vs. appointment doctor: The transcript distinguishes between the patient's 'primary doctor' (a fixed relationship) and the doctor assigned to an appointment ('the appointment is with a doctor'). It is not stated whether a patient can only be seen by their primary doctor in appointments, or whether they can see any doctor at the clinic. This affects whether the 'Appointment is with Doctor' role should be constrained to only the patient's primary doctor.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments. ... yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.
